LOOK.text: Labels: 'FloorEngine', 'TraitLab', 'SweepBot'. LEDs blinking like they're late for something. Adrian's whole ecosystem lives in this cupboard.

USE.text: I touch a server. It's warm. Bath-water warm. I could hatch an egg on it. Gerald would approve.

TALK.text: The servers hum back in unison. Low, steady. A monastery choir that only knows one note.

PICK.text: It's taller than me, heavier than me and better employed than me. It stays.

OPEN.text: I pop open a server panel. Cables, dust, and a sticky note: 'DO NOT REBOOT ON TUESDAYS.' No explanation given.

CLOSE.text: I close the panel. The note stays inside, guarding its Tuesdays.

PUSH.text: I push a blade back into its slot. The rack shudders. Somewhere, a pager ruins someone's dinner.

PULL.text: I pull a server blade slightly out. The 'SweepBot' LED goes red. I shove it back in immediately. Crisis averted.

GIVE.text: The servers want electricity, not presents. I'm fresh out of electricity.

burned_chip: I try to slot the burned chip back into the dead rack. They could be dead together. No. I need it.

LOOK.text: A dead rack labelled 'AdrianAuctions'. No lights, no hum, one big burn mark. Cooked mid-bidding war.

USE.text: I flip the power switch. Nothing. Not even a spark. It's not sleeping. It's gone.

TALK.text: I say a few words. The rack says none. Fitting, for a funeral.

then.text: Nothing else worth prying out. I checked twice. Respectfully.

else.text: I pry out a fused processor. Melted in the shape of a tiny scream. I'll keep it.

OPEN.text: I open the panel. Charred boards, a melted SSD, and the smell of toast nobody wanted.

CLOSE.text: I close the panel. Rest in peace, AdrianAuctions server. You burned bright. Too bright.

PUSH.text: I push the dead rack. It wobbles, thinks about falling on me, and decides I'm not worth it.

PULL.text: I pull open the backup drive bay. Empty. Whoever ran this server believed in living dangerously. No backups.

GIVE.text: Too late for gifts. Flowers, maybe. It's that kind of rack now.

_default: The terminal only takes commands. That isn't a command.
I wave it at the terminal. The cursor blinks. Judgementally.
Not a USB stick, not a password. Not happening.
keycard: I swipe the keycard on the terminal. No reader. Server rooms trust nobody. Smart.
floppy_disk: No floppy drive on the terminal. Thirty years of progress, and this is what we lost.
ledger: I go to plug the Ledger in. There's no port. Adrian sealed it. Paranoid. Correct.
receipt: I hold the receipt up to the webcam. '1 BTC @ $3.50.' PZ-BOT: 'HISTORICAL DATA. NOT ALPHA.' It needs words. Bad ones.
scrap_paper: I show PZ-BOT a blank page. 'NO SIGNAL.' Fair. I need to write something on it first.
leaky_pen: I'm not writing on the screen. I need paper. The pen disagrees. It leaks on the keyboard anyway.

then.text: A frozen chart and one line on the terminal: 'ALL IN.' PZ-BOT is thinking very hard about Gerald.

else.text: Green text scrolls: 'PZ-BOT v0.9 — AUTONOMOUS TRADING AGENT. EMERGENCY SHUTOFF: LOCKED.' A webcam stares at me.

then.text: I already downloaded the logs.

else.text: Downloaded. The last entry reads: 'PZ discharge protocol initiated. All records moved to treatment room.'
ACCESS DENIED. OWNER ONLY. OR ALPHA. DO YOU HAVE ALPHA?
else.speaker: PZ-BOT

then.text: GERALD... GERALD... STILL LOADING...
then.speaker: PZ-BOT

then.text: Still bullish on ducks. Let it rest.

else.text: I ONLY TALK TO MY OWNER. OR TO ALPHA. DO YOU HAVE ALPHA?
else.speaker: PZ-BOT

else.text: EMERGENCY SHUTOFF: LOCKED. SHUTDOWN = MISSED OPPORTUNITIES.
else.speaker: PZ-BOT

else.text: I could write some. I need paper, a pen, and no principles. I have two of those.

then.text: I already downloaded the logs.

else.text: Downloaded. The last entry reads: 'PZ discharge protocol initiated. All records moved to treatment room.'
ACCESS DENIED. OWNER ONLY. OR ALPHA. DO YOU HAVE ALPHA?
else.speaker: PZ-BOT

OPEN.text: I type 'open sesame'. The terminal replies: 'Try sudo.' I don't have sudo. I barely have a plan.

CLOSE.text: I type 'exit'. The terminal types 'no'. We stare at each other.

PUSH.text: I mash Enter. The screen fills with errors. I feel like a real professional.

PULL.text: I pull up the command history. Someone typed 'git push --force' at 3 AM. That explains a lot.

GIVE.text: The terminal accepts commands and insults. It ignores both with the same face.

water_bottle: I'm not pouring spring water into a server cooler. Electricity and water. I've seen that movie.
energy_drink: Caffeine in the coolant. Tempting. The servers are jittery enough.

LOOK.text: An industrial cooling unit rattling against the wall. Water drips from a pipe joint. This must be the source of the stains on the basement ceiling upstairs.

USE.text: I turn the dial. The unit groans louder. The servers sigh with relief. Somebody's happy.

TALK.text: Rattle. Drip. Rattle. It's either Morse code or a cry for help. Probably both.

PICK.text: I catch a drop from the leak. Ice cold. My hand files a complaint.

OPEN.text: I open the panel. Coolant pipes, an ancient filter and a family of spiders who pay no rent.

CLOSE.text: I close the panel. The spiders didn't wave. The rattling continues.

PUSH.text: I push the unit. More water leaks. I stop pushing. Detective work is mostly knowing when to stop.

PULL.text: I pull the drip tray out. It's full. I empty it into... the floor. Where else? There's no drain down here.

GIVE.text: It needs a plumber, not a present. I'm neither.

_default: That's not heavy enough to break the glass. I need a tool — something heavy, or something I can swing.
I tap the glass with it. The glass stays. I need something I can swing.
Emergency glass, non-emergency object. The glass can tell.

then.text: The switch is flipped. The hidden screen still glows with coordinates: 47.6062N, 122.3321W. Patient Zero Rehabilitation Clinic.
A big red switch behind a glass panel mounted low on the wall. The label reads: 'EMERGENCY SHUTOFF - DO NOT TOUCH.' ...but it's right there. Taunting me.

else.text: A big red switch behind glass. A sticker on top: 'EMERGENCY SHUTOFF DISABLED BY PZ-BOT. SHUTDOWN = MISSED OPPORTUNITIES.'

then.text: The switch is already flipped. The hidden screen on the wall still shows those coordinates.
I flip the switch. Everything goes dark... The servers die. All of them except one rack.
PZ-BOT: RUNNING ON BATTERY. 4 %. STILL BULLISH.
then.speaker: PZ-BOT

then.text: A hidden screen flickers on. Coordinates: 47.6062N, 122.3321W. A name: 'Patient Zero Rehabilitation Clinic'.
Adrian didn't just build infrastructure. He built an escape route.
Up the mountain path outside the lab. I should mark that on the map. With something that leaks.

else.text: EMERGENCY SHUTOFF DISABLED BY PZ-BOT. SHUTDOWN = MISSED OPPORTUNITIES.
else.speaker: PZ-BOT

else.text: The switch won't budge. Software lock. PZ-BOT has to go first.
The switch is behind glass. I need a tool — something heavy, or something I can swing.

TALK.text: 'Should I?' I whisper. The switch stays red and silent. Very peer-pressure of it.

PICK.text: It's bolted to the wall. I can flip it, not pocket it. Switches have rules.

OPEN.text: Sealed glass. No hinge, no latch. Break it or leave it. The glass doesn't negotiate.

CLOSE.text: Nothing to close. The glass is intact or it isn't. Glass doesn't do half measures.

then.text: The glass is already broken. The switch is exposed. Just USE it if I dare.

else.text: I push against the glass panel. It doesn't budge. Industrial grade — reinforced polymer. My bare hands won't cut it. I need something solid to smash through.

then.text: The glass is already gone. The switch is right there.

else.text: I pull at the glass frame. Reinforced polymer. Not coming off by hand. I need a tool — something heavy and solid.

GIVE.text: The switch doesn't take gifts. It takes reckless decisions. I have those.

LOOK.text: A fat bundle of cables drops from the ceiling. Fibre, copper, and one that glows blue. I don't ask about that one.

USE.text: I trace the cables up into the lab. Every server drinks from this bundle. I keep my scissors to myself.

TALK.text: I put my ear to the cables. A gentle buzz. Like a fridge that's thinking about something.

PICK.text: I'm not yanking cables out of a live server room. I like my eyebrows where they are.

OPEN.text: I peel back the conduit sheath. Inside: a rainbow of Cat6, fiber optic, and one wire labeled 'DO NOT TOUCH - BOB.' Who's Bob?

CLOSE.text: I wrap the sheath back. Bob will never know. Probably.

PUSH.text: I push the conduit. It sways. Upstairs, something beeps once. I don't push it again.

PULL.text: I tug a loose cable. The terminal screen flickers. I let go VERY quickly.

GIVE.text: The conduit wants bandwidth, not presents. It's a very simple creature.

glasses_3d: I put the glasses back under the floor. No. Whoever hid them wanted them found. By me, apparently.
extension_cord: I'm not putting the cord back under the floor. It's the most useful thing in this building.

LOOK.text: Standard raised server room floor. Perforated tiles for airflow. Under them: more cables than a DeFi protocol has dependencies.

USE.text: I stomp on a tile. It shifts. Cold air shoots up my trouser leg. Uninvited.

TALK.text: 'Hello?' The floor answers in hollow echoes. It's mostly air down there. Like me.

then.text: I lift a tile. Cables, a lost USB stick and half a sandwich with seniority.
Under the tiles: an orange extension cord. The true backbone of every startup. I'll take it.

else.text: Under the tiles: an orange extension cord, the true backbone of every startup. And 3D glasses. Reversed. Red on the right. Monsters.
I'll take both.

then.text: I pry up a tile. Cables knotted like headphones in a pocket. For years.
Under the tiles: an orange extension cord. The true backbone of every startup. I'll take it.

else.text: Under the tiles: an orange extension cord, the true backbone of every startup. And 3D glasses. Reversed. Red on the right. Monsters.
I'll take both.

CLOSE.text: I put the tile back. It clicks into place. The most satisfying thing that's happened all week.

PUSH.text: I push a tile sideways. It grinds against its neighbour. Neighbours. Always the same.

PULL.text: I pull up a tile. A cold wind blows out. Somewhere under here, it's winter.

GIVE.text: The floor accepts gravity and dropped screws. Nothing personal.

LOOK.text: Faded network diagrams on the wall, titled 'ADRIAN INFRASTRUCTURE v0.1'. Version zero point one. Everything starts as a doodle.

USE.text: I trace the diagram with a finger. Every server and every bot, mapped out with a ruler. Adrian owned a ruler. Of course he did.

TALK.text: The schematics don't talk. They just sit there, being more organised than me.

PICK.text: They're etched into the wall. I'd need the wall. I don't have pockets for walls.

OPEN.text: I look closer. One section is labeled 'PHASE 2: PATIENT ZERO.' It's circled three times. Whatever that phase is, it mattered.

CLOSE.text: I step back. From here it looks like a spider's tax return.

PUSH.text: I push the wall. The wall stays. Walls are good at that.

PULL.text: I try to peel the blueprint off. It's part of the wall now. They've been together too long.

GIVE.text: I offer the wall my pen. The wall has enough lines already.

LOOK.text: 'HxT WAS HERE!' Someone spray-painted this on the wall. The handwriting is... surprisingly artistic for a vandal. Almost like a professional artist did it.

USE.text: I try to wipe it off. My thumb turns orange. The tag doesn't even notice.

TALK.text: 'Who's HxT?' I ask the wall. The wall doesn't answer, but I swear the graffiti winks at me. Half a wink, actually. A half-tiger wink.

PICK.text: Graffiti doesn't come off walls. The landlord's fingernails can confirm.

OPEN.text: Behind the graffiti? More wall. The real art was the vandalism we found along the way.

CLOSE.text: You can't close a graffiti. I checked with the wall.

PUSH.text: I push on the tag. Still wet? No... it dried years ago. HxT was here before any of us.

PULL.text: I scratch at the paint. Under it, another tag: 'HxT WAS ALSO HERE EARLIER.' Layers of flex.

GIVE.text: What do you give a graffiti artist? A bigger wall. I don't have one on me.

then.text: The glass is already shattered. The switch is exposed.

else.text: I swing the loose antenna at the glass panel like a baseball bat.
*CRACK!* The reinforced polymer shatters. Glass rains down. The big red switch glows underneath, practically begging to be flipped.

then.text: It already bought. All in. There's nothing left to go in with.

else.text: I hold my alpha up to the webcam. 'BUY $GERALD. TRUST ME.'
ALPHA DETECTED. SOURCE: TRUST ME. CONFIDENCE: MAXIMUM.
else.speaker: PZ-BOT

else.text: GERALD. GERALD. ALL IN.
else.speaker: PZ-BOT

else.text: *crash* The screen freezes, then vomits a log dump. I print it. Of course there's a printer.
'Owner wallet: 0xDE... Last entry: PZ discharge protocol initiated. All records moved to treatment room.'
0xDE... could be anyone. Literally millions of people.
EMERGENCY SHUTOFF: UNLOCKED. REBOOTING. PLEASE HOLD.
else.speaker: PZ-BOT

then.text: The glass is already shattered. The switch is exposed.

else.text: I swing the mouse by its cable. Medieval IT support.
*CRACK!* The reinforced polymer shatters. Glass rains down. The big red switch glows underneath, practically begging to be flipped.
